{{Short description|Distance between two probability measures in statistics}}

In [[statistics]], '''Bhattacharyya angle''', also called '''statistical angle''', is a measure of distance between two [[probability]] measures defined on a finite probability space.  It is defined as

: <math> \Delta(p,q) = \arccos \operatorname{BC}(p,q) </math>

where ''p''<sub>''i''</sub>, ''q''<sub>''i''</sub> are the probabilities assigned to the point ''i'', for ''i''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''n'', and

: <math> \operatorname{BC}(p,q) = \sum_{i=1}^n \sqrt{p_i q_i} </math>

is the '''Bhattacharya coefficient'''.<ref>{{Cite journal|title = On a measure of divergence between two statistical populations defined by their probability distributions|last = Bhattacharya|first = Anil Kumar|date = 1943|journal = Bulletin of the Calcutta Mathematical Society|volume = 35|pages = 99–109}}</ref>

The Bhattacharya distance is the [[geodesic distance]] in the [[orthant]] of the sphere <math>S^{n-1}</math> obtained by projecting the probability simplex on the sphere by the transformation <math>p_i \mapsto \sqrt{p_i},\ i=1,\ldots, n</math>.

This distance is compatible with [[Fisher metric]]. It is also related to [[Bures metric#Bures distance|Bures distance]] and [[Quantum fidelity|fidelity]] between [[quantum state]]s as for two diagonal states one has

: <math>\Delta(\rho,\sigma) = \arccos \sqrt{F(\rho, \sigma)}.</math>
